svg.title: Master bedroom air-handler node: PROTO-SHIELD layout
svg.text: Master bedroom air-handler node: parts on the Olimex PROTO-SHIELD rev A, component side
To scale, 11 px per mm. Solid parts and the red 5 V rail are on the component side; dashed wires run on the solder side, drawn as seen through the board.
Coordinates in mm from the board's bottom-left corner, as on Olimex's mechanical drawing. Proto columns c1–c13 run left to right, rows r1–r14 top to bottom.
Bare 22 AWG solid tinned wire on the
component side: up c6 from the 5V
along r1 to c13. Solder it only where a
lead lands: c6 r1, r12 and r14, c7 r1, c13 r1.
Between the pad columns the shield runs
C6 and C7 take ground from the GND bus
between c11 and c12 (b11). The terminals'
bridged on the solder side and each runs
to the GND cluster top left.
Each header pin has two duplicate pads
beside it. Terminal wires land on the
outer one, parts on the inner one.
c6's neighbours are the GND bus (left)
and the 3V3 bus (right). Keep solder on
the rail's pads small. Leave the CON
Parts: R7 4.7 kΩ D2 pull-up; R8, R9 10.0 kΩ 0.1 % NTC dividers; R10 1 kΩ D8 pull-up; C6, C7 0.1 µF on A0, A1. The shield's own R1–R6 and C1–C5 are why ours start at R7 and C6.
Terminal pins sit in the outer column of CON-A/CON-B through-holes (1A, 3A … 15A, 2B, 4B, 6B), 2.54 mm apart, wire entries facing off the left edge.
Before soldering, ring with a meter: the 5V, A0, A1, D2 and D8 duplicate pads to their header pins, and the top-left cluster to GND.
